Intesa Sanpaolo stock: MPS offer sets January 22 deadline
sum: Intesa Sanpaolo moved its planned acquisition of Banca Monte dei Paschi di Siena into a defined timetable on November 10, 2026. In a press release, the bank said it had published the offer document and the EU follow-on prospectus for its voluntary public tender and exchange offer for all ordinary shares of Banca Monte dei Paschi di Siena.

The acceptance period is scheduled to begin at 8:30 a.m. Italian time on November 24 and end at 5:30 p.m. on January 22, 2027, unless extended. The consideration comprises 1.250 euros and 1.664 newly issued Intesa Sanpaolo shares for each MPS share tendered. Payment is scheduled for January 29, 2027, subject to the conditions set out in the offer documents.

On November 11, Intesa Sanpaolo made available its interim statement for the period ended September 30. The release was listed on the bank's investor-relations website. The document adds a reporting milestone to a week dominated by the MPS transaction.

Intesa Sanpaolo stock traded at 6.29 euros on Lang & Schwarz at 11:39 CET on Saturday, November 14, around 0.02 percent below the Xetra close of Friday, November 13. The stock's Xetra close rose 1.85 percent over the week, from 6.177 euros on Friday, November 6, to 6.291 euros on Friday, November 13, according to Investing.com.

For investors, the next clearly defined milestones are the start of the MPS acceptance period and the scheduled payment date. The transaction terms and the interim statement remain the key company-specific reference points for assessing execution and capital-market implications.
Italian equities traded against the broader FTSE MIB market backdrop.

Intesa Sanpaolo stock sets MPS offer window from November 24
sum: Intesa Sanpaolo published the offer document and the EU follow-on prospectus for its voluntary public tender and exchange offer for Banca Monte dei Paschi di Siena on Tuesday, November 10. The bank said the acceptance period will run from November 24, 2026, through January 22, 2027, unless extended. The timetable gives investors a defined next step in the proposed combination with MPS.

The details were set out in Intesa Sanpaolo's press release. CONSOB approved the offer document and the EU follow-on prospectus on November 8, before the documents were published. The prospectus covers the admission to trading of the new Intesa shares issued to service the offer.

Under the published terms, holders who tender one MPS share will receive 1.250 euros in cash and 1.664 newly issued Intesa Sanpaolo shares. The offer covers all MPS ordinary shares, with a maximum of 3,037,594,735 shares subject to the offer after deducting 823,448 MPS shares held by Intesa Sanpaolo as of the offer document date.

The acceptance window opens at 8:30 a.m. Italian time on November 24 and closes at 5:30 p.m. Italian time on January 22. Intesa Sanpaolo said payment is scheduled for January 29, 2027, unless the period is extended. The dates are therefore relevant for MPS shareholders assessing whether and when to tender.

Intesa Sanpaolo also said it would voluntarily apply the provisions for reopening the acceptance period if the relevant requirements are met. Unless the timetable is extended, the possible reopening would cover five trading sessions from February 1 through February 5, 2027. Payment for shares tendered during that period would be scheduled for February 12.

The transaction remains subject to the procedures and restrictions set out in the offer documents. Intesa Sanpaolo stated that the offer is promoted in Italy and that investors should read the offer document and prospectus before assessing the terms.

Intesa Sanpaolo stock traded at 6.28 euros on Lang & Schwarz at 11:48 CET on Friday, November 13, 2026, 0.48 percent above the Xetra close of Thursday, November 12. The comparison uses the prior Xetra session because the current quote was recorded before the same day's Xetra close.

Intesa Sanpaolo Balances Record Earnings Against ECB Caution on MPS Takeover
sum: Intesa Sanpaolo has published the offer document and the EU follow-on prospectus for its takeover of all shares in Banca Monte dei Paschi di Siena, clearing the way for the next procedural stage of a transaction valued at EUR 34.5 billion. Italy's market regulator Consob approved the document on Monday. The acceptance period is scheduled to run from 24 November 2026 to 22 January 2027, unless extended.

The filing also sets out the terms Intesa would apply to any future offer for Mediobanca shares it does not yet hold through MPS. Those terms would follow the exchange conditions approved earlier by the boards of both MPS and Mediobanca in March. A full acquisition of Mediobanca is a precondition for delisting and complete integration, and any such offer depends on the MPS takeover succeeding first — a link that ties the prospects of both deals together.

The operational backdrop is forceful. On 3 November the bank reported a net profit of EUR 8.2 billion for the first nine months of 2026, of which more than EUR 2.6 billion came in the third quarter alone. Management raised its full-year 2026 net profit guidance to well above EUR 10 billion. Alongside those results, Intesa resolved an interim dividend on 2026 earnings of EUR 0.22 per share before tax, payable on 25 November, with the cash payout totalling EUR 3.813 billion.

That combination of earnings momentum and shareholder returns is what analysts are weighing against the demands of the takeover. DZ Bank reiterated its buy recommendation on Monday, with analyst Philipp Häßler pointing to the stronger-than-expected record third-quarter result, the raised annual outlook and the MPS deal proceeding to plan. The firm did trim its fair value estimate, however, to EUR 7.20 from EUR 7.40. The stock slipped 1.2% on Monday to close at EUR 6.33.

The decisive yardstick comes from the European Central Bank. According to a Reuters report on Tuesday, the ECB, in clearing the MPS acquisition, urged caution on dividends and called for adequate capital buffers, citing the complexity of the transaction and its implementation risks. That guidance puts the focus squarely on how much financial headroom the deal will absorb — and how much remains for distributions.

Banca Monte dei Paschi di Siena stock gets takeover timetable
sum: Banca Monte dei Paschi di Siena stock is heading toward a formal takeover timetable after Intesa Sanpaolo said on November 8 that CONSOB had approved the offer document and the EU follow-on prospectus. The announcement sets the next key dates for shareholders.

According to the Intesa Sanpaolo press release, the acceptance period is scheduled to run from 8:30 a.m. Italian time on November 24, 2026, through 5:30 p.m. on January 22, 2027. The period may be extended under the applicable rules.

If the offer conditions are fulfilled or waived and the transaction closes, Intesa plans to pay each participating MPS shareholder 1.25 euros in cash plus 1.664 newly issued Intesa Sanpaolo shares for every MPS share tendered. Payment is scheduled for January 29, 2027, the fifth trading day after the end of the acceptance period.

Intesa also said it would voluntarily apply the reopening mechanism if the relevant requirements are met. In that case, shareholders could tender during five trading sessions from February 1 through February 5, 2027, with payment scheduled for February 12.

The offer covers up to 3,037,594,735 MPS shares, excluding 823,448 shares already held by Intesa Sanpaolo. The new Intesa shares would be admitted to trading on Euronext Milan. The offer document also states that the MPS issuer notice required under Italian takeover rules will be disclosed separately by the bank.

On Lang & Schwarz, Banca Monte dei Paschi di Siena stock traded at 11.49 euros at 10:39:03 Berlin time on Wednesday, November 11, 2026. Investors are likely to focus on the conditions of the offer, the cash-and-share mix and the response from MPS shareholders as the acceptance window approaches.

Unipol stock enters earnings phase as Berenberg holds target
sum: Unipol is entering a new earnings phase after completing its EUR 2.5 billion rights offering, while Berenberg kept its EUR 33.50 price target despite cutting earnings forecasts for 2026 through 2028.

In a note discussed by Finimize, Berenberg said Unipol could absorb higher weather-related claims and bond-market effects that weakened its solvency ratio in the third quarter. The bank still expects the insurer to remain on track for its 2027 objectives, including a 92 percent combined ratio and mid-single-digit premium growth in non-life and life insurance over 2024-2027.

Berenberg reduced its net income and adjusted operating earnings-per-share forecasts for 2026 through 2028 but left its price target unchanged. That combination places greater emphasis on whether investors accept a higher valuation multiple despite near-term claims and solvency volatility.

The rights offering involved 121,582,320 new shares and raised EUR 2.50 billion. The larger equity base gives Unipol more financial flexibility, but future earnings per share will depend on how effectively the group deploys the proceeds.

Unipol is also reshaping its banking interests. The company plans to acquire 635 Banca Monte dei Paschi di Siena branches from Intesa Sanpaolo and transfer them to BPER Banca in exchange for a larger stake, making execution and capital allocation important factors for the investment case.
Unipol stock traded at 26.29 euros on Lang & Schwarz at 18:02 CET on Tuesday, November 10, 2026.

That was 1.62 percent above the 25.87 euros cited in the November 9 report at 11:50 CET. Upcoming financial disclosures should show how the enlarged capital base affects earnings per share and whether operating performance remains consistent with the 2027 targets.

Trump's midterm defeat: Europe's biggest stock winners and losers
sum: A Democratic ‘blue tsunami’ sparked one of the year’s sharpest rotations in Europe: banks rallied, chips sank on data-centre fears.
When Americans voted last week, European investors were watching one question above all: how much room would Donald Trump have left to govern?
Democrats took control of both the House of Representatives and the Senate, a clear defeat for the US president halfway through his term.
On trading floors, the result quickly earned a name: the "blue tsunami".
At first glance, Europe's stock market barely reacted. The Stoxx 600 jumped 1.8% on Wednesday, then gave most of it back. By Friday's close it stood just 0.4% above Tuesday's level.
The Euro Stoxx 50, which tracks the euro area's 50 largest companies, followed the same path. It rose 2% on Wednesday and ended the week just 0.4% higher.
Look beneath the surface, though, and it was one of the most violent reshuffles of the year.

sum: Mitsubishi Heavy Industries, Ltd. engages in the development, manufacture, and sale of energy systems in Japan, the United States, Asia, Europe, Central and South America, Africa, the Middle East, and internationally. It operates through Energy Systems; Plants & Infrastructure Systems; Logistics, Thermal & Drive Systems; and Aircraft, Defense & Space segments. The company offers thermal power generation systems, such as gas turbine combined cycle and steam power systems; nuclear power generation systems, including light-water reactors, nuclear fuel cycle and advanced solutions; wind power generators; engines for aircrafts; compressors; and marine machinery. It also provides metals machinery; commercial ships; engineering systems, such as transportation system and chemical plant; environmental systems; and machinery systems include paper converting machinery, intelligent transport systems, and test equipment. In addition, the company offers air-conditioning and refrigeration systems, engines, turbochargers, and automotive thermal systems; carrier systems and specialized carriers; industrial AC equipment and centrifugal chillers; car air-conditioning; box making and paper converting; and cargo carriers. Additionally, it provides commercial aviation, defense aircraft, missile systems, naval ships, maritime systems, special vehicles, tanks, and space systems; movable equipment for cultural and sports; seismic isolation and vibration control equipment; piping and pumps; industrial heat pumps; industrial AC equipment and centrifugal chillers; data centers; and CO2 capture solutions, exhaust gas treatment systems, water and sludge treatment systems, water treatment and recycling systems, marine generator turbines, boilers and exhaust gas recovery power generation equipment, and oil storage barges. Further, the company offers post-operational services for nuclear power plants. Mitsubishi Heavy Industries, Ltd. was founded in 1884 and is headquartered in Chiyoda, Japan.

Banca Monte dei Paschi di Siena stock lifts outlook after strong Q3
sum: Banca Monte dei Paschi di Siena reported a stronger third quarter and lifted its 2026 profit outlook on Friday, November 6, as the Italian lender continued to navigate Intesa Sanpaolo's takeover bid.

Borsa Italiana reported net profit of 543 million euros for the third quarter, up 14.6 percent from a year earlier. Nine-month net profit increased 21.2 percent to 1.657 billion euros, while revenue rose 5.6 percent to 6.023 billion euros.

Pre-provision profit reached 1.161 billion euros in the quarter, an increase of 14.8 percent year on year. For the first nine months, pre-provision operating profit climbed 10.2 percent to 3.461 billion euros. Third-quarter revenue was 1.998 billion euros, below the 2.065 billion euros recorded in the previous quarter.

Management raised its 2026 profit-before-tax guidance to above 3.7 billion euros. The bank also reported a fully loaded CET1 ratio of 16.4 percent, providing a substantial capital buffer as strategic uncertainty remains high.

Shareholders rejected the management-backed defensive plan on Thursday, October 29, clearing a major obstacle for Intesa Sanpaolo's proposed takeover. The vote leaves regulatory approvals and the offer process as the next major milestones for investors.

Banca Monte dei Paschi di Siena stock traded at 11.22 euros on Lang & Schwarz at 11:23 CET on Saturday, November 7, 2026. Investors can follow the real-time quote of Banca Monte dei Paschi di Siena stock.

Intesa Sanpaolo stock: MPS exchange ratio raised after dividend decision
sum: Intesa Sanpaolo has adjusted the share exchange ratio in its voluntary public tender and exchange offer for Banca Monte dei Paschi di Siena after approving an interim dividend. The bank's official press release, issued on Tuesday, November 3, 2026, raises the ratio to 1.664 newly issued Intesa Sanpaolo shares for each MPS share, from 1.600 previously.

The adjustment offsets the effect of the 22-euro-cent interim dividend, which is scheduled to detach on November 23 and be paid on November 25. The offer remains subject to the conditions and procedures set out in the offer documents, while Intesa Sanpaolo said it will continue to inform the market about developments.

In a separate Intesa Sanpaolo investor-relations release, the bank reported net income of 8.199 billion euros for the first nine months of 2026, up 8.1 percent from the comparable period. Third-quarter net income reached 2.645 billion euros.

Intesa Sanpaolo raised its 2026 net income outlook to well above 10 billion euros. Operating income rose 5 percent to 21.457 billion euros in the nine-month period, while operating costs declined 1.3 percent to 7.876 billion euros. The cost-to-income ratio improved to 36.7 percent.

The Common Equity Tier 1 ratio stood at 13.1 percent at September 30 after the amount accrued for distribution was deducted from capital. The company said 7.8 billion euros had been accrued for distribution in the first nine months, including 3.8 billion euros for the interim dividend, alongside a 2.3 billion euro buyback completed in October.

The results strengthen the financial backdrop for the MPS transaction and the planned shareholder distribution, but the offer's final outcome will depend on the formal offer process and market participation. For investors, the revised ratio links the dividend decision directly to the share-based consideration offered to MPS shareholders.

sum: AUSTIN, Texas, Nov. 2, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Oracle Corporation (ORCL) today announced the pricing of concurrent underwritten public offerings of 86,206,897 shares of its common stock, par value $0.01 per share, at a public offering price of $116.00 per share (the "common stock offering") and $2,000,000,000 of its 7.000% notes due 2029, $1,750,000,000 of its 7.450% notes due 2031, $2,250,000,000 of its 7.850% notes due 2033, $2,500,000,000 of its 8.000% notes due 2037 and $1,500,000,000 of its 8.650% notes due 2046 (the "notes offering" and, together with the common stock offering, the "offerings").

Each of the offerings is expected to close on November 4, 2026, subject to customary closing conditions. The completion of the common stock offering is not contingent on the completion of the notes offering, and the completion of the notes offering is not contingent on the completion of the common stock offering.

The net proceeds from the common stock offering will be approximately $9.9 billion, after deducting the underwriting discounts and Oracle's estimated offering expenses. The net proceeds from the notes offering will be approximately $10.0 billion, after deducting the underwriting discounts and Oracle's estimated offering expenses.

The net proceeds of the offerings, if completed, will be used for general corporate purposes, which may include capital expenditures, repayment of indebtedness, future investments or acquisitions and payment of cash dividends on or repurchases of our common stock.

BofA Securities is acting as sole global coordinator of the offerings. Wells Fargo Securities, Citigroup, BNP PARIBAS, Deutsche Bank Securities, J.P. Banca Monte dei Paschi di Siena stock: Vote clears Intesa path
sum: Shareholders of Banca Monte dei Paschi di Siena rejected CEO Luigi Lovaglio's defence proposals against Intesa Sanpaolo's takeover bid at a meeting on Thursday, October 29, 2026. Banca Monte dei Paschi di Siena stock traded at 10.92 euros on Lang & Schwarz at 15:00 CET on Monday, November 2, 2026.

The result removes the central elements of management's plan to counter Intesa's proposed 33-billion-euro takeover through acquisitions of Banco BPM and wealth manager Banca Generali. The vote also changes the balance between MPS's standalone expansion strategy and Intesa's offer.
According to ANSA, more than 91 percent of the capital represented at the meeting voted against the Banco BPM transaction. The proposal received 6.47 percent support, while 2.41 percent abstained.

The Banca Generali proposal was rejected by 90.9 percent of the represented capital, with 6.66 percent in favour and 2.41 percent abstaining. Shareholders also voted against the proposed merger with Mediobanca: 63.65 percent opposed it, 32.91 percent supported it and 3.42 percent abstained.

For investors, the failed transactions reduce management's ability to build an independent banking group around MPS, Banco BPM and Banca Generali. Intesa's offer therefore becomes the dominant strategic issue, although the shareholder vote itself does not complete a takeover.

Europe close: Banks, chip stocks pull markets lower
sum: European stocks fell sharply on Thursday as weakness in the banking and chip sectors provided a big drag on regional indices.

The pan-European Stoxx 600 index was down 1.1% at 637.73, with heavy losses in Milan, Madrid and Paris in particular showing significant losses given their heavy weighting towards banks, which fell as a result of a sell-off of European government bonds.

French 10-year OAT yields climbed further above the 5% level, up 7.5 basis points at 5.076% to hit their highest since 2002, due to rising fiscal and political concerns. The sell-off saw borrowing costs rise elsewhere in the eurozone, with 10-year yields rising in Germany, Italy and Spain.

Meanwhile, Brent crude was up 2.2% at $111.18 a barrel and West Texas Intermediate was 1.3% stronger at $98.37, after Houthi attacks in Saudi Arabia heightened fears that the conflict in the Middle East was intensifying.

In equity movements, Milan-listed banks UniCredit, Intesa Sanpaolo, Banco BPM, BPER and Monte dei Paschi all fell sharply, along with Madrid-listed peers Santander, BBVA, CaixaBank, Sabadell and Bankinter.

London's Barclays fell as it reported a slightly lower-than-expected third-quarter profit due to weakness in the fixed income division, as it announced a £500m share buyback and confirmed plans to cut around 5,000 jobs this year in an AI push.
Semiconductor stocks also fell across the board amid renewed AI investment concerns, including heavyweights ASML, Infineon and STMicroelectronics.

sum: - Intesa Sanpaolo added €800 million in cash, or €0.25 per share, to its Monte dei Paschi offer, valuing the bid at roughly €35 billion.
- Delfin, MPS’s largest investor with 17.6%, will tender its stake and vote against the MPS defense plan on October 29.
- Intesa pays mostly in its own shares, which trade at 1.68x book value on a 16.27% return on equity in Q2 2026.
Intesa raised its bid while paying mostly in its own stock. Track ISP’s valuation and returns as the MPS vote nears on TIKR for free →

On the H1 2026 earnings call last July 29, Intesa Sanpaolo (ISP) CEO Carlo Messina said there was “0 possibility that we will increase our price” for Monte dei Paschi di Siena (BMPS). Ten weeks later, Intesa did.

It added €0.25 per MPS share in cash, or €800 million, on top of 1.6 new Intesa shares per MPS share. That raises the cash payment per MPS share by 25%, from €1 to €1.25, while increasing the overall offer’s value by about 2.3%, using Friday’s Intesa closing price to value the share component.
The extra cash comes with a condition. MPS shareholders must reject CEO Luigi Lovaglio’s defense plan on October 29, and Intesa said it will drop the bid entirely if that plan passes.

items.t: INTESA SANPAOLO: LONG-TERM INCENTIVE PLANS
sum: Turin - Milan, 12 June 2026 – At its meeting today, the Board of Directors of Intesa Sanpaolo decided to execute the Bank’s 2026-2029 Long-term Incentive Plans, which are based on financial instruments. The Plans, detailed as follows, were approved at the Shareholders’ Meeting held on 30 April 2026:

- the “2026-2029 Performance Share Plan” Long-term Incentive Plan reserved for all the Management, including the Managing Director and CEO, the remaining Top Risk Takers and the other Risk Takers of the Group both in Italy and abroad (“PSP”);
- the “2026-2029 LECOIP” Long-term Incentive Plan reserved for all the other employees, meaning the Professionals, of the Group in Italy (“LECOIP”).
In execution of today’s resolution of the Board of Directors, Intesa Sanpaolo on 30 June 2026:
(i) with regard to the LECOIP, will execute the capital increases to serve the Plan (through the issue of the related shares);

(ii) with regard to the PSP, will assign to each manager the PSP Rights, each of which confers the right to accrue, at the end of the Plan, one Intesa Sanpaolo share, provided that the conditions laid down in the Plan’s regulations are met and in compliance with the limits of number and amount as set at the above-mentioned Shareholders’ Meeting.

Intesa Sanpaolo renews partnership with the Ellen MacArthur Foundation
sum: Intesa Sanpaolo renews its decade-long Strategic Partnership with the Ellen MacArthur Foundation through a new four-year agreement, to strengthen the shared commitment to advancing the circular economy as a driver of industrial competitiveness, economic resilience and resource security.

The Ellen MacArthur Foundation is a leading global advocate for the transition to a circular economy, and Intesa Sanpaolo will continue the collaboration to accelerate this shift, including through initiatives supporting the development of a favourable regulatory framework, starting with the forthcoming European Circular Economy Act.

“Over the past ten years, we have demonstrated that the circular economy is a transformative paradigm for the economic system, a driver of innovation, investment, competitiveness and growth. Our commitment has been tangible, translating into financial instruments and open innovation initiatives supporting a large number of companies engaged in the transition”
Paola Angeletti, Chief Sustainability Officer of Intesa Sanpaolo and Chair of Intesa Sanpaolo Innovation Center

Intesa Sanpaolo translates the circular economy into concrete financial instruments. Under the 2022 - 2025 Business Plan, the Group provided €15.9 billion in financing to support the transition from linear to circular models, in addition to the €7.7 billion delivered under the 2018 - 2021 Business Plan.

The new 2026 - 2029 Business Plan confirms Intesa Sanpaolo’s commitment to the circular economy within the broader framework of sustainable financing, which is expected to account for 30% of total new lending.

The collaboration with the Ellen MacArthur Foundation, of which Intesa Sanpaolo has been the first financial services Strategic Partner in the Foundation’s Network since 2016, , has contributed to the definition of validation criteria for credit lines dedicated to the circular economy.

Massimo Zanetti Beverage Group at the centre of a potential sale
sum: MILAN – There is talk of a potential sale of Massimo Zanetti Beverage Group (MZBG) – one of the world’s leading players in the production, processing and distribution of roasted coffee. The company ended 2025 with revenues of €1.3 billion and an operating profit of €86 million. A controlling stake –up to 100% – in the Group is reportedly on the table, with the deal potentially valuing the company at around one billion.

According to rumours reported in the media, the main shareholders — the QuattroR fund and entrepreneur Massimo Zanetti — have entrusted investment banks Lazard and Intesa Sanpaolo-Imi with the search for new investors.
Sources suggest interest from European operators, particularly from Central Europe, already active in the food or drinks sectors
Massimo Zanetti Beverage Group operates in 110 countries and has 20 production facilities in Europe, Asia and the Americas. It boasts 40 brands and employs over 3,000 people.
Plans up to 2028 forecasts revenue growth of 8–10% on average per year, reflecting the company’s renewed vitality.
The company returned to profit last year thanks to a turnaround plan launched in 2023, when the QuattroR fund acquired a 50% stake.

Under the leadership of the new CEO Pierluigi Tosato, the Group has streamlined its operations (including the closure of its Greek operations) and relaunched the historic Segafredo brand, one of the most popular in Italy.

items.t: Intesa Sanpaolo at salone del mobile.milano 2026 to support design and the made in italy supply chain
sum: - €26 billion disbursed to SMEs in the Made in Italy sector since 2020
- Event at Gallerie d’Italia on Made in Italy and presentation of the volume “Le fabbriche del design”
- On 23 April, appointment at the Salone pavilions with Intesa Sanpaolo’s talk on finance and competitiveness in the furniture-design sector

Milan, 8 April 2026 – Intesa Sanpaolo, Institutional Partner of Salone del Mobile.Milano, renews its commitment to supporting design companies and the home & living sector with the event: “Design e Made in Italy. Il supporto di Intesa Sanpaolo all’impresa italiana e alla visione creativa sulla scena globale” (“Design and Made in Italy. Intesa Sanpaolo’s support for Italian enterprise and creative vision on the global stage”), scheduled today at 5.30 pm at the bank’s museum, Gallerie d’Italia-Milan.

This initiative forms part of the support initiatives that the Bank has pursued for years for the design sector and, more broadly, for Made in Italy, a supply chain comprising thousands of SMEs representing excellence in production and creativity recognised internationally.

The collaboration with Salone del Mobile.Milano, launched in 2017, represents a concrete tool to support companies in the design and home & living sector. This commitment also sees Intesa Sanpaolo active through the Supply Chain Development Programme, which today involves over 240 Made in Italy supply chains, more than 32,000 employees and almost 7,700 suppliers, with turnover exceeding €32 billion in the furniture, clothing, food and automation sectors.

The programme, launched by the Group ten years ago, has been extended to all Italian manufacturing sectors and over time has enabled SMEs to strengthen access to credit and more effectively support investments in innovation, digitalisation, sustainability and the circular economy, while supporting them in their growth and expansion into international markets.

sum: Italian private bank Fideuram - Intesa Sanpaolo Private Banking has acquired the remaining shares of REYL Intesa Sanpaolo held by François Reyl, chief executive Pasha Bakhtiar, Christian Fringhian and Lorenzo Rocco di Torrepadula, representing in total 24 percent of the bank’s share capital.
As a result, Intesa Sanpaolo’s private banking division now holds full ownership and control of REYL Intesa Sanpaolo.
